manifest.name: dsh-edit-panel
manifest.description: Live writing panel for DeepSeek Harness: the AI writes a text or Markdown file section by section into a right-sidebar editor where you can type at the same time; rewrites of existing text become proposals you keep or refuse change by change.
manifest.author: Mathieu Portmann

bundle.text:
# dsh-edit-panel bundle: text and Markdown files written live, section by section, in a
# right-sidebar tab where the user can edit them at the same time. Removing the bundle
# removes all of it.
- insert:
    - id: edit-panel
      name: 'dsh-edit-panel'
      config: {}

readme.text:
Live writing of text files for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/AI-Scarlett/DSH-Store) (DSH):
the AI writes a text or Markdown file section by section into an editor in the right sidebar, and
you can type in the same file at the same time.

> **Maintenance: best-effort.** Issues may go unanswered; forks are welcome.

- **Five tools for the model**, in every conversation:
  - `edit_begin(path, outline, title?)` creates the file with its headings and opens the panel;
  - `edit_write_section(section, content)` writes one section, saved to disk at once;
  - `edit_status()` says what is written, what you changed, and what to do next;
  - `edit_finish()` ends the draft;
  - `edit_open(path)` shows an existing file in the panel without changing it.
- **The panel** (a right-sidebar tab, *Live writing*): each section in a small word-processor editor
  (bold, italic, headings, lists, quotes, links, undo; read and written as Markdown). What you type is
  saved after a short pause, and the AI cannot overwrite a section while you are typing in it.
- **Proposals instead of overwrites**: when the AI rewrites a section that already has text, the
  file does not change; the panel shows its proposal word by word (added in green, removed struck in
  red), and you keep or refuse each change, or all of them.
- **Existing files are safe**: an existing file is drafted in `<file>.draft` and replaces the original
  only when you press **Finish** (the original is copied to the backup folder first); **Cancel**
  discards

Files: `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.text`, `.tex`, `.org`, `.rst`, `.qmd`, `.rmd`, inside your home
folder and not in a hidden folder. In Markdown files, sections are the `## ` headings.

The interface is in English, and in French when DSH's language is French (tables `en` and `fr` at
the top of `client.js`).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:MathieuPortmann/dsh-edit-panel
```

Restart the profile afterwards. Requires Node `^22.19.0 || >=24` and DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0` (see
[Compatibility](#compatibility)). Once the package is on npm, `dsh plugin --profile web add
dsh-edit-panel` works too.

Options of the `edit-panel` row:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dataDir` | `<DSH_HOME>/edit-panel` | state of the drafts (one JSON per conversation) and the document list |
| `backupDir` | `<DSH_HOME>/backups/edit-panel` | copies of files before they are replaced or opened |
| `announce` | `true` | one line in every conversation telling the model that text files are written through the panel; set `false` to use the tools only when asked |

- `lib/draft.js` holds the drafts: it renders the file from its sections, reads it back to see
  what you changed (a fingerprint per section), keeps proposals waiting, locks a section for 30 s
  while you type, and replaces or restores files with backups. `lib/docs.js` keeps the document
  list. Both are pure Node.js and covered by `tests/`.
- `index.js` (host side) registers the tools, sends the draft state as runtime context, and serves
  the panel through an RPC channel at `/edit-api/<method>`, behind DSH's own connection check.
- `client.js` (page side) draws the tab, the drawer and the editors. The editor itself
  (`web/editor.js`) is a bundle of [ProseMirror](https://prosemirror.net) and
  [markdown-it](https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it) built from `web-src/editor.js`; the
  page receives it from the host and loads it once.

| Component | Supported |
|---|---|
| Node.js | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` (`engines.node`) |
| DSH | `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`; declared as optional `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, the only DSH packages the host side imports |
| Platform | Linux (tested); pure JavaScript, no native addon |
| Page | DSH's web UI with the right sidebar; the drawer finds the message box by its editable area and may need an update when the page changes |

| Capability | Where | Used for | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Files** | `lib/draft.js`, `lib/docs.js` | writes the text files the model drafts and the files you open in the panel, **only inside your home folder, never in hidden folders, only the text extensions above**; `<file>.draft` working copies; backup copies in `backupDir`; state in `dataDir` | the tool or the panel shows the error; nothing is written |
| **Network** | none | nothing leaves the computer | n/a |
| **Commands** | none | no child process, no shell | n/a |
| **Tools for the model** | `index.js` | `edit_open`, `edit_begin`, `edit_write_section`, `edit_status`, `edit_finish` (see above) | an error text is returned to the model |
| **HTTP route** | `index.js` (`ctx.webServer.register`) | `POST /edit-api/<method>` for the panel, behind `ctx.connection.admit()` (DSH's Host/Origin fence and token); JSON bodies only, limited to 1 MiB | non-admitted requests get 401/403; other errors are returned in the RPC envelope |
| **Dynamic module loading** | `index.js` (`importFromDsh`) | loads `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` from the DSH installation that runs the plugin. Nothing is downloaded | th

Checked on a disposable profile (`DSH_HOME` pointing at a temporary folder, so the real profile is
never touched):

```sh
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile t add file:$PWD/dsh-edit-panel-0.1.0.tgz   # install
dsh t --port 3095 --no-open                                      # start: plugin loads, no error
dsh plugin --profile t remove dsh-edit-panel                      # uninstall

`npm test` runs 9 standalone tests (drafts: new and existing files, the user's edits, locks,
proposals kept, merged or refused, open in place, cancel, duplicate headings, path rules; the
document list) with no DSH installation needed.

`web/editor.js` is reproducible: `cd web-src && npm ci && npm run build` rebuilds it byte for byte
with the versions pinned in `web-src/package-lock.json` (esbuild 0.28.2). The bundled libraries and
their licenses are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

```sh
npm test
cd web-src && npm ci && npm run build   # after changing web-src/editor.js
```

MIT for this plugin. The bundled libraries keep their own licenses (MIT, and BSD-2-Clause for
`entities`), see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
